notes:
Account background: Midport Converse Works builds an embedded conversational layer for product analytics dashboards used by PMs and CSMs. Initial contact via developer trial (Hosted API) in Oct 2025; moved to small POC to validate latency/throughput and embedding quality. POC results: average generative latency ~120ms p50, p99 ~240ms on Hosted; embeddings pipeline (batching) stable at 80–120 req/s with 13ms per vector on test runs. Customer targets: sustained 50 QPS (chat) during business hours, bursts up to 200 QPS for feature launches; embedding throughput target 200 req/s for nightly re-index.

Timeline / recent activity (shorthand):
- 2025-10-20: Signed up for Hosted free credits — AE Jordan intro.
- 2025-11-03: Demo + architecture review (Fireflies ff_2025-11-03_midport_intro). They asked about VPC/private control plane.
- 2025-11-15: POC kickoff — small corpus (~2M tokens/day equivalent), test prompt set for product guidance flow.
- 2025-12-08: POC review: quality ok on Llama-variant verified model; latency numbers above. SE Priya tuned batching and KV cache; documented in POC results drive doc.
- 2026-01-20: Commercial discussion started — they want Dedicated for predictability/data isolation.
- 2026-02-09: Pricing call with procurement, legal intro (Fireflies ff_2026-02-09_pricing-call). Presented draft commit tiers and ramp schedule.

Requirements summary (from product/infra leads):
- Workload: interactive chat + contextual summarization + nightly reindex embeddings.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms for standard chat paths.
- Throughput: sustained 50 QPS; burst up to 200 QPS for 1–4 hour windows.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; wants predictability and clear overage math.
- Model preferences: open-weight Llama-style variants or Redwood-verified models; flexibility to route to cheaper quantized variants for lower-criticality paths.
- Routing/fallback: require automatic fallback to smaller model if Dedicated capacity constrained (policy defined by customer).
- Security: SSO/SAML, audit log retention 13 months, KMS integration for key management, EU data residency for subset of customer data.

Pricing/packaging negotiation points (detailed):
- Customer prefers Dedicated reserved capacity. Proposed commercial terms discussed:
  - Base commit: 2x midsize GPU nodes (approx equivalent to 2 A100-80GB class) reserved; baseline monthly fee proposed $15,000/mo for 12-month term.
  - Commit bandwidth mapped to throughput: baseline covers up to 50 sustained QPS and 2M embedding vectors/day; includes 10% burst buffer.
  - Ramp schedule: Month 1 = 25% commit credit, Month 2 = 50%, Month 3 = 75%, Month 4+ = 100% commit. Credits applied prorata to monthly fee for first 3 months.
  - Burst pool: Allow bursts up to 2.5x baseline for up to 6 hours/month at preferential burst rate (40% of on-demand increment cost) — priced to avoid surprise bills.
  - Overage: After burst allowance, overage billed per 1k tokens or per 1k embedding units (customer requested both views). Draft overage shown as $0.045 / 1k tokens for generation and $0.005 / embedding vector (example numbers — under legal review).
  - Ramp credits: First-quarter ramp credit of 20% off month fees if usage remains below commit for first 3 months (to ease adoption).
  - SLA and uptime: 99.9% uptime for control plane, 99.5% for inference latency SLOs with service credits on misses.

Customer feedback / negotiation asks (open):
- Wants clearer worked examples showing monthly bill at 50 QPS baseline vs. spike events—AE to deliver a 3-scenario bill simulation.
- Needs a firm statement on EU data residency segmentation (which parts can be resident in EU) and proof of SOC2 + ISO artifacts.
- Requests optional add-on: longer audit log retention (24 months) — cost TBD.
- Procurement asked for a 24-month term option with reduced monthly rate; Redwood offered 12- and 24-month pricing; customer to indicate preference.

Next steps (actionable):
- AE Jordan to deliver bill simulation (3 scenarios) and revised SOW with ramp credit language by 2026-02-20.
- SE Priya to produce technical note on VPC peering + KMS flow and embed in security FAQ doc (due 2026-02-18).
- Legal to share draft SOW and customer to route to procurement (expected review week of 2026-02-22).
- Follow-up pricing call scheduled 2026-02-28 (tentative) — objective: lock commit level or get procurement counter.

Short-term risks: procurement wants more conservative commit; product leads worry about unpredictable feature launch bursts. Discussed mitigations: scheduled burst reservations and ability to autoscale to on-demand with pre-agreed caps.
